goodThing.fits: Saturday, a day for the woods; Germany's forest is a third of the country and still growing.
goodThing.headline: A third of Germany is forest, and it is growing
goodThing.line: The 2024 national forest count: up 15,000 hectares since 2012. Pine, spruce, beech and oak, in that order.

onThisDay.fits: 26 September 1887: Emile Berliner, born in Hanover, filed his gramophone patent.
onThisDay.headline: A man from Hanover invented the record player
onThisDay.line: Emile Berliner filed his patent for the gramophone: sound on a flat disc, not a cylinder. Every record since is his idea.

calmRead.fits: Saturday evening before a German Sunday, when everything closes; the reason is in the constitution.
calmRead.title: Why Germany goes quiet on Sundays
calmRead.teaser: The shops shut, the drills stop, and it is all written into the constitution.
paragraphs: Tomorrow morning the supermarkets in {city} will be dark, the drills and lawnmowers silent, and the streets slower. Visitors find it strange. Germans find it normal, and most of them would fight to keep it.

The rule is older than the country. Article 139 of the Weimar constitution of 1919 says that Sunday and the public holidays remain protected by law as days of rest from work and, in a lovely phrase, of spiritual uplift. When the Federal Republic wrote its Basic Law in 1949, it kept that sentence alive, word for word, through Article 140.

So Sunday rest is not a habit or a shop policy. It is constitutional. Courts have struck down attempts to open shops on too many Sundays. Bakeries are allowed a few hours in the morning, because a Sunday without fresh rolls was judged a hardship. Almost everything else waits until Monday.

The point is not religion any more, if it ever entirely was. The point is that everyone has the same day off. You cannot be asked to work, so nobody can ask you to shop, so the family can sit down together, and the neighbour cannot mow.
Buy the bread today. Tomorrow, do nothing, on purpose, with the whole country.

word.meaning: Coffee, cake and unhurried talk with friends, ideally on a Saturday afternoon. Klatsch is the sound of chatter.
